Turn around regularly and inspect how the return route looks from that direction. Record intermediate coordinates at every major turn. Do not depend on individual Torches that may disappear among trees or hills.

Return home when the Sun is clearly descending, half the food or Torches are gone, or orientation no longer feels reliable. Begin another stage the next morning.

Set the checkmark only after seeing several connected buildings or Villagers from a safe distance. Do not immediately run inside.
task.firsttorch.305ac7e92f61bd84.title: Discovered a possible Village from a safe distance
quest.firsttorch.village.approach.title: Recognise the Village
quest.firsttorch.village.approach.descri:
Goal: check in daylight whether you have really found a Village.

A Village usually consists of several generated buildings and paths. Villagers live there; Beds, workstations, small farms, and a Bell are also common. An Iron Golem may guard the Village, but one is not always visible or present.

Villages look different in different landscapes. Houses may use other materials and roofs, while paths can break or shift on steep terrain. One house, well, or path alone therefore does not prove that a Village is present.

Remain outside the buildings at first and observe the area. Do not enter in darkness, and do not attack a Villager or Iron Golem. Do not open a Chest or remove a Bed or workstation yet.

Set the checkmark after recognising at least two of these features together: several buildings, paths, Villagers, farms, a Bell, or an Iron Golem.
task.firsttorch.527ce90b4183dfa6.title: Recognised several clear Village features
quest.firsttorch.village.record.title: Secure the Village Location
quest.firsttorch.village.record.descript:
Goal: make the discovered Village reliably findable again.

Stand at a visible edge of the Village and record X, Y, and Z outside the world. Add a short description such as ‘Village by the river’ or ‘Village beyond the Birch forest’ so the numbers remain identifiable later.

Mark the safe approach sparingly with a Sign, small Cobblestone marker, or several Torches. Do not build in the middle of a Village path or block a door. If you arrived by Boat, record the safe landing place as well and either collect the Boat or leave it clearly visible on land.

Check the first section of the return route afterwards. If darkness approaches, return home and visit again the next morning. The inhabitant lesson does not require staying through the night.

Set the checkmark when the Village coordinates and description are recorded and the safe return route or landing place is recognisable.

Reward: 5 experience points for discovering a Village that you can also find again.
task.firsttorch.749e0b2d63a5f1c8.title: Recorded the Village coordinates and marked the return route
quest.firsttorch.village.respect.title: Behave Carefully in the Village
quest.firsttorch.village.respect.descrip:
Goal: move safely and respectfully through the Village.

Do not attack a Villager or the Iron Golem. A Golem protects the Village and may retaliate after an attack. Do not continue fighting if that happens: run away, gain distance, and return carefully later.

Leave Beds and workstations where they are. Do not open a Village Chest yet or harvest an entire field. These things support the inhabitants’ routine and will make more sense in later lessons.

Right-clicking the Bell rings it. The sound can send Villagers into their houses. Try it no more than once, and do not block doors or paths.

Set the checkmark after observing the Village without attacking an inhabitant or removing one of its important blocks.
task.firsttorch.25daf83b6c714e09.title: Explored the Village carefully and respectfully
chapter.firsttorch.trading.title: Trading and Returning Home (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.trading.description: Understand professions and offers, trade thoughtfully and return safely.
trophy.firsttorch.trading.title: A Good Trade
trophy.firsttorch.trading.description: You traded and safely completed your Village expedition.
image.firsttorch.villager_trading.descri: Trading screen with an example offer; actual offers may differ.
quest.firsttorch.trading.professions.des:
Goal: find an adult Villager with a profession and the matching workstation.

An unemployed adult Villager can claim an available, reachable workstation during the day. Their clothing changes to match the profession; opening the trading screen also shows the profession.

Examples: Composter = Farmer, Lectern = Librarian, Blast Furnace = Armorer, and Brewing Stand = Cleric. You do not need to craft or move a block for this lesson.

Baby Villagers cannot trade yet. An adult Villager wearing green is a Nitwit and will not take a profession.

Before the first trade, a Villager may lose the profession again if the workstation is removed. After a completed trade, the profession and unlocked offers remain. Leave the Village workstations in place.

Set the checkmark after recognising one employed Villager and the matching workstation.
task.firsttorch.47fc1a5d0e936b2c.title: Recognised a Villager and the matching workstation
quest.firsttorch.trading.offers.title: Read the Trading Screen
quest.firsttorch.trading.offers.descript:
Goal: open the trading screen of an adult Villager with a profession and understand one offer.

Right-click the Villager to open the trading screen. The offers appear on the left. Required items go into the input slots; the item you receive appears in the result slot on the right.

The image shows only an example: 20 Wheat are exchanged for one Emerald. The Villager’s actual offers are authoritative and may look different.

Emeralds are the main trading item used by Villagers. They are not a universal currency for every part of Minecraft.

The bar at the top shows the Villager’s profession experience. Trading can raise their level and unlock more offers.

Set the checkmark when you can identify the cost and result of one offer. You do not need to buy anything yet.
task.firsttorch.691e3c7f20b58d4e.title: Understood the cost and result of a trade offer
quest.firsttorch.trading.trade.title: Complete Your First Trade
quest.firsttorch.trading.trade.descripti:
Goal: trade with a Villager for the first time. This is detected automatically.

Choose an offer with a cost you can spare. Do not spend your last food, important tool, or rare material merely to complete this task.

Place the requested items into the input slots and take the result from the right-hand slot. That completes the trade.

An offer can temporarily sell out after several uses. The Villager can restock it at their reachable workstation. Prices and available offers can change.

Reward: four Torches for the journey home and 5 experience points for your first trade.
task.firsttorch.0b305e912d74af60.title: Completed the first trade with a Villager
quest.firsttorch.trading.leave.title: End the Village Visit Safely
quest.firsttorch.trading.leave.descripti:
Goal: leave the Village safe and begin the journey home in time.

Place no more than a few Torches along clearly dark paths or immediately outside exposed house entrances. Do not remove Village blocks or try to illuminate every house completely. Close an open Wooden Door with right-click, but never wall up or block an entrance – Villagers must still be able to enter and leave.

Ordinary enemies can appear in and around Villages wherever it is dark enough. Zombies are especially dangerous to Villagers; Skeletons, Spiders, and Creepers also make a night-time stay hazardous.

You are not required to fight a group of enemies to save the Village. Retreat when darkness is already arriving. If the route home is no longer safe, close yourself temporarily inside an empty building or a small shelter of your own and wait for daylight. Do not remove a Bed or workstation.

Before leaving, check that you have not blocked a door, path, or workstation. Set the checkmark once you can leave the Village in daylight or have a safe plan for waiting.
task.firsttorch.5c81b27e4fa3d609.title: Left the Village safely without trapping its inhabitants
quest.firsttorch.trading.return.title: Return Home Deliberately
quest.firsttorch.trading.return.descript:
Goal: return safely to your base along the planned route.

Compare your current position with the recorded Village and home coordinates. Follow the known approach first, then use your landmarks or intermediate coordinates. Check regularly that X and Z are actually changing in the intended directions.

If you arrived by Boat, collect it again at the marked shore or use it for the return journey. Leave a deliberately stored Boat clearly visible on land so it cannot drift away and remains easy to find on the next visit.

Keep food and several Torches ready. Do not rush blindly through a dangerous shortcut or begin a long leg shortly before night. Return to the last known point if you become uncertain.

Set the checkmark only after reaching your base using the Village note, coordinates, and known route.
task.firsttorch.7ea3d49061c5f82b.title: Returned home using the Village note and known route
quest.firsttorch.trading.finish.title: Complete the Village Expedition
quest.firsttorch.trading.finish.descript:
Goal: organise your travel inventory and keep a complete Village note.

Store collected resources and trading items in suitable Chests. Repair or replace badly worn tools before the next outing. Food, Torches, and a Boat may remain together as a prepared travel kit.

Add the Village coordinates, a short route description or memorable intermediate points, and the safe landing place if one exists to your note. Also record an interesting trade that you may want to find again later.

Keep the note outside your world or as a labelled Book or Sign at the base. A memory such as ‘somewhere beyond the forest’ is rarely enough after several in-game days.

Set the checkmark when your inventory is ready again and the Village location is documented clearly enough for a later visit.

Reward: three Bread for provisions and 5 experience points for your first fully completed expedition.
task.firsttorch.10c5f6b283e71a4d.title: Organised the travel inventory and kept a complete Village note
chapter.firsttorch.deep_mining.title: Your First Diamonds
chapter.firsttorch.deep_mining.descripti: Prepare a safe descent and craft your first Diamond Pickaxe.
trophy.firsttorch.deep_mining.title: Diamonds Safely Recovered
trophy.firsttorch.deep_mining.descriptio: You completed the path to your first Diamond Pickaxe.
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.equipment.d:
Goal: hold all equipment for a longer deep-mining trip in your inventory at the same time.

Bring two Iron, Diamond, or Netherite Pickaxes, one Water Bucket, one Shield, 32 Torches, and eight cooked foods. Two suitable Pickaxes prevent one broken tool from leaving you stuck deep underground.

Keep Water, Shield, food, and Torches in easy-to-reach slots. Leave several inventory spaces empty and store anything you do not need at home first.

Tasks count your supplies without consuming them. Completed tasks stay recorded; check that you still carry everything before departure. Stronger Pickaxes you already own count too.

Reward: Four Bread as an extra reserve for the long journey home.
task.firsttorch.2d5fb17380c49e6a.title: Hold 2 Iron-or-better Pickaxes
task.firsttorch.3e60c28491d5af7b.title: Hold 1 Water Bucket
task.firsttorch.4f71d395a2e6b08c.title: Hold 1 Shield
task.firsttorch.5082e4a6b3f7c19d.title: Hold 32 Torches
task.firsttorch.6193f5b7c408d2ae.title: Hold 8 cooked foods
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.coordinates:
Goal: find your coordinates and record the entrance to your safe return route.

Press F3 to open the debug screen. Some keyboards also require Fn. Find the X Y Z or Block line. X and Z describe your horizontal position; Y is your height.

Write down the X, Y, and Z coordinates of your cave entrance or the top of your safe staircase. A Compass needle does not automatically point to your home, so it cannot replace this note.

The lower the Y value becomes, the deeper you are. Below Y 0 is the deep part of the Overworld. Close the debug screen with the same key after reading the values.

Mark the checkmark when you have found the Y value and recorded your return-route coordinates.
task.firsttorch.03b517d9e62af4c0.title: Y value read and return-route coordinates recorded
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.deepslate.d:
Goal: collect 16 Cobbled Deepslate.

Follow a safe staircase downward. Deepslate appears increasingly between Y 8 and Y 0; below Y 0, most of the ground is made from it. The dark rock takes longer to mine than ordinary Stone.

Mine Deepslate with a Pickaxe. It enters your inventory as Cobbled Deepslate. Never dig straight down, and keep using your familiar Torch rule for the journey home.

Turn back before your final suitable Pickaxe nearly breaks. The 16 blocks automatically prove that you reached the deep layer safely.

Reward: Eight Torches replace some of the lighting used during the descent.
task.firsttorch.25d739fb084c16e2.title: Hold 16 Cobbled Deepslate
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.tunnel.titl: A Safe Search Tunnel for Diamonds
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.tunnel.desc:
Goal: prepare a lit search tunnel with a safe return route at approximately Y −53.

Diamond Ore generates below Y 16 and becomes more common deeper down. Around Y −53 is a practical compromise: deep enough for a good search, but above many large Lava areas and farther from Bedrock. The value does not guarantee a find.

Make a two-block-high main tunnel with short side tunnels. Keep placing Torches on the right while travelling inward. This exposes more rock without creating one enormous open room.

Mine only as far ahead as you can safely see. If you hear Lava or see light through a gap, stop and open the area sideways from a safe distance. Keep the Water Bucket ready.

Mark the checkmark when the search tunnel is lit and you can find its exit using the Torches and your coordinate note.
task.firsttorch.47f951bd2a6e3804.title: Prepared a safe, lit Diamond search tunnel
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.diamonds.de:
Goal: hold three Diamonds in your inventory at the same time.

Diamond Ore has bright blue flecks in Stone or Deepslate. Mine it only with an Iron, Diamond, or Netherite Pickaxe. A weaker tool destroys the block without dropping a Diamond.

Do not immediately mine every visible Ore block. Light the area and first remove neighbouring blocks while standing on a safe surface. Check especially below the Ore for Lava or a deep opening.

Pick up every dropped Diamond. Keep the first three until the task completes; you will use them for your first Diamond Pickaxe next.

Reward: 5 experience points for your first safe Diamond discovery.
task.firsttorch.691b73df4c805a26.title: Hold 3 Diamonds in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.deep_mining.pickaxe.des:
Goal: craft a Diamond Pickaxe.

Return home safely with the Diamonds. Place three Diamonds across the top row of the Crafting Table. Put one Stick in the centre of both the middle and bottom rows.

The shape is the same as your earlier Pickaxes. A Diamond Pickaxe lasts longer and can mine Obsidian; you can still use cheaper tools for ordinary Stone.

Reward: 5 experience points and one Golden Apple. Save the Apple for real danger; eating it temporarily grants extra golden hearts and supports healing.
task.firsttorch.0b3d95f16ea27c48.title: Own a Diamond Pickaxe
chapter.firsttorch.enchanting.title: Enchanting Foundations
chapter.firsttorch.enchanting.descriptio: Turn your first Diamonds into a safe, practical enchanting setup.
trophy.firsttorch.enchanting.title: First Enchantment
trophy.firsttorch.enchanting.description: You built an Enchanting Table and enchanted your first item.
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.obsidian.des:
Goal: hold four Obsidian in your inventory at the same time.

Approach Lava only from a safe surface. Place Water beside the Lava so it flows across the top. When Water touches a still Lava source block, it creates Obsidian. Flowing Lava may produce Cobblestone instead; this is not an error.

Leave the Water in place at first. Do not stand on the Obsidian block you are mining, and check the edges for more Lava. Mine Obsidian only with your Diamond Pickaxe or a better tool.

Mining takes much longer than ordinary Stone. Hold the left mouse button until the block breaks completely, then collect it. The Water can immediately cover Lava exposed underneath.

Reward: 5 experience points for handling Water and Lava safely.
task.firsttorch.2e60c28491d5af7b.title: Hold 4 Obsidian in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.sugar_cane.d:
Goal: hold three Sugar Cane in your inventory at the same time.

Sugar Cane commonly grows beside shores. The plant stands on a suitable block directly next to Water and can become several blocks tall. Break the upper parts but leave the bottom part in place so it grows again later.

Plant extra Sugar Cane by right-clicking Dirt, Grass, Sand, or another suitable block directly beside Water. It does not need Farmland.

Keep at least three Sugar Cane at the same time. You will turn them into Paper next.

Reward: One Leather for your first Book. This means you do not have to kill one of your protected breeding animals just for this lesson.

When you obtain Leather yourself later, Cows and Horses are common sources: they can drop Leather when killed. Never sacrifice your final breeding pair. For Cows, use only a surplus adult after at least two adults remain safe in the pen.
task.firsttorch.5193f5b7c408d2ae.title: Hold 3 Sugar Cane in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.book.title: Paper and Your First Book
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.book.descrip:
Goal: craft one Book.

Place three Sugar Cane next to each other in one horizontal row of the crafting grid. This makes three Paper.

Then place the three Paper and the rewarded Leather in any free slots. The Book recipe is shapeless, so the exact arrangement of these four ingredients does not matter.

Take the Book from the result slot. An Enchanting Table needs exactly one Book. More Books will become useful for Bookshelves later.
task.firsttorch.04c628eaf73b05d1.title: Own 1 Book
image.firsttorch.paper_and_book.descript: Three Sugar Cane make Paper; three Paper and one Leather make a Book.
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.lapis.title: Lapis Lazuli for Enchanting
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.lapis.descri:
Goal: hold three Lapis Lazuli in your inventory at the same time.

Lapis Lazuli Ore has strong dark-blue flecks in Stone or Deepslate. It occurs underground and can be mined with a Stone Pickaxe or a better tool.

One Ore block usually drops several Lapis Lazuli. Collect at least three and keep them. One choice at the Enchanting Table will later cost between one and three Lapis Lazuli.

Do not confuse Lapis Lazuli with Diamonds: Diamond Ore is lighter and turquoise-blue, while Lapis Lazuli Ore is much darker.

Reward: 5 experience points to prepare you for your first enchantment.
task.firsttorch.26e840ac195d27f3.title: Hold 3 Lapis Lazuli in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.table.title: Build the Enchanting Table
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.table.descri:
Goal: craft one Enchanting Table.

In addition to the Book and four Obsidian, you need two more Diamonds. Find and secure them with the same careful method as before.

Put the Book in the top-centre slot. Place one Diamond on each side of the middle row with one Obsidian between them. Fill the entire bottom row with the other three Obsidian.

Take the Enchanting Table from the result slot and place it somewhere safe at home. Leave space around it for now; Bookshelves will improve its options later.

Reward: 5 experience points for building your first enchanting station.
task.firsttorch.591b73df4c805a26.title: Own 1 Enchanting Table
image.firsttorch.enchanting_table_recipe: Recipe for an Enchanting Table: one Book, two Diamonds, and four Obsidian.
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.first.title: Your First Enchantment
quest.firsttorch.enchanting.first.descri:
Goal: enchant an item for the first time. This is detected automatically.

Open the Enchanting Table with right-click. Put an unenchanted, enchantable item in the left slot and Lapis Lazuli in the right slot. A cheap tool is suitable for your first attempt; you do not have to use the Diamond Pickaxe immediately.

In the image, 1 marks the item, 2 marks the Lapis Lazuli, and 3 marks the three possible offers.

Up to three offers appear on the right. You need at least the experience level shown. The top, middle, and bottom choices also consume one, two, or three Lapis Lazuli and respectively one, two, or three experience levels.

Choose an affordable offer and remove the enchanted item. Without Bookshelves, the offered enchantments are deliberately weak; improving the setup comes next.

Reward: 10 experience points and three Lapis Lazuli for more attempts.
task.firsttorch.7b3d95f16ea27c48.title: Enchant an item at the Enchanting Table
image.firsttorch.enchanting_interface.de: Enchanting Table screen: 1 item, 2 Lapis Lazuli, and 3 the three possible offers.
chapter.firsttorch.library.title: Bookshelves and Enchanting
chapter.firsttorch.library.description: Expand your Enchanting Table with Bookshelves and inspect its strongest offers.
trophy.firsttorch.library.title: Complete Enchanting Station
trophy.firsttorch.library.description: You built a full Bookshelf setup around your Enchanting Table.
quest.firsttorch.library.first_bookshelf:
Goal: craft one Bookshelf.

Open the Crafting Table. Fill the top and bottom rows with three Wooden Planks of any type each. Place three Books across the middle row.

Take the Bookshelf from the result slot. One shelf already improves the Enchanting Table slightly; its strongest offers later require a total of 15 effective Bookshelves.

Reward: Three Books replace the Books used in the first shelf and help with the remaining expansion.
task.firsttorch.51a4d8fc0637eb92.title: Own 1 Bookshelf
image.firsttorch.bookshelf_recipe.descri: Bookshelf recipe: three Wooden Planks above and below three Books.
quest.firsttorch.library.complete.title: A Complete Small Library
quest.firsttorch.library.complete.descri:
Goal: hold 15 Bookshelves in your inventory at the same time.

Fifteen Bookshelves require 90 Wooden Planks and 45 Books in total. The 45 Books need 135 Paper and 45 Leather. Your first shelf and the three rewarded Books already count toward this total.

Build this supply gradually. Harvest your renewable Sugar Cane repeatedly and replant enough of it. Prefer surplus adult Cows for Leather after at least two adult breeding animals remain safe in the pen. Horses can also provide Leather.

You only need to hold all 15 shelves at the same time once so the task can detect them. You may place them during the next step afterward.

More than 15 effective Bookshelves do not increase the strength of one Enchanting Table any further.
task.firsttorch.62b5e90d1748fca3.title: Hold 15 Bookshelves in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.library.station.title: The Complete Enchanting Station
quest.firsttorch.library.station.descrip:
Goal: arrange 15 effective Bookshelves around the Enchanting Table and inspect its offers.

Place the shelves two blocks away from the Enchanting Table. This leaves exactly one empty block between the Table and each shelf. Shelves may stand at the same height as the Table or one block higher.

The plan shows the setup from above: the Table is in the centre, the orange outlined ring stays completely empty, and 15 shelves stand outside it. The opening at the bottom is the entrance. Do not put a Torch, Carpet, or another block in the gap.

Open the Table and insert an enchantable item. With 15 effective shelves, the bottom offer can reach level 30. You need to have at least 30 experience levels to select it; purchasing it then consumes only three levels and three Lapis Lazuli.

Enchantment offers remain random and do not always reveal every resulting effect before selection. Set the checkmark after checking the setup and seeing a level-30 offer. You do not have to buy it yet.

Reward: 10 XP points and three Lapis Lazuli for your expanded station.
task.firsttorch.73c6fa1e28590db4.title: Placed 15 effective shelves and saw a level-30 offer
Top-down plan: an Enchanting Table with one empty block around it and 15 Bookshelves outside that gap.
chapter.firsttorch.nether_portal.title: A Safe Portal Frame
chapter.firsttorch.nether_portal.descrip: Prepare the site and build an unlit Nether Portal frame without entering yet.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_portal.title: Portal Frame Ready
trophy.firsttorch.nether_portal.descript: You prepared and checked an unlit Nether Portal frame.
quest.firsttorch.nether_portal.site.desc:
Goal: understand the Nether's most important differences and choose a safe place for the portal frame.

The Nether is another dimension. It has no normal daytime, many areas contain fire or Lava, and new hostile creatures await you. Build and check everything in the familiar Overworld first.

Important: Water from a Bucket cannot be placed normally in the Nether; attempting it makes the Water evaporate immediately. Never use a Bed there—it explodes instead of setting a respawn point.

Choose a flat place near home with solid ground. Keep away from storage Chests, fields, and animal pens so the arrival area remains clear. Leave enough space in front of and behind the future portal for safe arrival.

Only during the ignition attempt should the immediate ignition area remain clear of wood, leaves, and other flammable blocks. If ordinary fire appears instead of the purple portal surface, you can extinguish it safely and check the frame. A successfully activated portal does not set its surroundings on fire.

This first section builds only the frame. Do not light it or walk through yet. The complete equipment and safe return routine come before the first visit.

Set the checkmark after choosing a suitable portal site with clear and safe access.
task.firsttorch.135ad6029fb74ce8.title: Chose a safe portal site with clear access
quest.firsttorch.nether_portal.flint.des:
Goal: hold one Flint in your inventory.

Gravel is a grey, grainy block that falls downward like Sand. Never dig directly beneath a Gravel ceiling. Clear it from the side or above and keep one open step behind you.

A Shovel mines Gravel especially quickly. Breaking it usually drops Gravel again, but sometimes produces Flint instead. This is random; if Gravel drops, you can place it again and continue mining it.

Pick up one Flint. The task completes automatically as soon as it is in your inventory.
task.firsttorch.357cf824b1d96e0a.title: Own 1 Flint
quest.firsttorch.nether_portal.flint_and:
Goal: craft one Flint and Steel.

Open your inventory with E. Place one Iron Ingot and the Flint in any two slots of the small 2 × 2 crafting grid. The recipe is shapeless; the two items do not have to lie diagonally as shown in the image.

Take the Flint and Steel from the result slot. Right-clicking can light a fire on a suitable block. Do not test it inside your house, against a wooden wall, in a forest, or beside your supplies—fire can spread.

You can put out a single fire block with the left mouse button, even with an empty hand; no tool is required. Do not step into the flame, and extinguish only fire you can reach from safe ground.

Keep the Flint and Steel, but do not use it on the portal frame yet.

Reward: One Iron Ingot replaces the Iron used for the Flint and Steel.
task.firsttorch.579e1a46d3fb802c.title: Own 1 Flint and Steel
image.firsttorch.flint_and_steel.descrip: Flint and Steel recipe: one Iron Ingot and one Flint in any arrangement.
Ten Obsidian for the Smallest Frame

Goal: hold ten Obsidian in your inventory at the same time.

Obtain Obsidian with the same safe Water-and-Lava method used for the Enchanting Table. Let Water flow over still Lava source blocks and mine the resulting Obsidian only with a Diamond or Netherite Pickaxe.

Ten Obsidian are enough for the smallest working portal frame because its four corners may remain empty. A fully filled rectangular frame requires 14.

Crying Obsidian has conspicuous bright purple areas and may occur in Ruined Portals. It looks similar, but cannot be part of an activatable Nether Portal frame.

Hold all ten ordinary Obsidian in your inventory at the same time. The task does not consume them.

Reward: 5 XP points for gathering the materials carefully.
task.firsttorch.0ac14d79062eb35f.title: Hold 10 Obsidian in your inventory at the same time
quest.firsttorch.nether_portal.frame.des:
Goal: build an unlit Nether Portal frame at the prepared site.

The smallest frame stands vertically and measures four blocks wide and five blocks tall on the outside. Its opening is two blocks wide and three blocks tall.

The image shows a finished frame made from exactly ten Obsidian. Place the two bottom Obsidian blocks first, then both three-block-tall sides, and finally the two top blocks. Use safe stairs or Scaffolding to reach the top instead of simply jumping down.

The four Dirt blocks in the image are only temporary building blocks at the corners; they are not part of the portal frame itself and may be removed after construction. The corners do not require Obsidian.

Later, you will use Flint and Steel to light a fire on the lower inside of the frame. Keep the immediate ignition area clear of flammable blocks until activation succeeds. If only ordinary fire appears instead of the purple portal surface, extinguish it immediately with the left mouse button and check the frame. An active portal does not spread fire by itself.

Do not use the Flint and Steel yet. First check that the frame is stable and has clear ground on both sides.

Set the checkmark after building and checking the frame.

Reward: Eight Torches and 5 XP points for the prepared portal site.
task.firsttorch.3df470ac3951e682.title: Safely built an unlit 4 × 5 portal frame
image.firsttorch.nether_portal_frame.des: Smallest Nether Portal frame: 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks high outside, using 10 Obsidian without its corners.
chapter.firsttorch.nether_equipment.desc: Prepare, activate, and secure a portal without entering the Nether.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_equipment.title: Ready at the Portal
trophy.firsttorch.nether_equipment.descr: You prepared the portal and completed the final readiness check without entering.
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.gold.t: Five Gold Ingots for the Journey
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.gold.d:
Goal: hold five Gold Ingots at the same time.

Gold Ore has yellow inclusions in Stone or Deepslate. Mine it only with an Iron, Diamond, or Netherite Pickaxe. Without Silk Touch it drops Raw Gold; smelt Raw Gold in a Furnace with fuel to make Ingots.

Keep five Ingots together until the task completes. In the next step, make a Golden Helmet from them.

Reward: Four Coal as fuel reserve.
task.firsttorch.25d2e7f3ab60841c.title: Hold 5 Gold Ingots at the same time
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.helmet:
Goal: craft a Golden Helmet and put it on.

Fill the top row of the Crafting Table with three Gold Ingots. In the row below, place one Ingot on the left and right while leaving the middle slot empty. Take the Helmet, then equip it in the highest armour slot.

Ordinary Piglins do not attack merely because you are present while you wear one piece of Gold Armour. This is not complete protection: attacks and some actions still anger them, and Piglin Brutes attack regardless. Wear your best available Armour in the other slots.

Set the checkmark while the Helmet is equipped.

Reward: Five Gold Ingots and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.58051a26de93b74f.title: Own a Golden Helmet
task.firsttorch.69162b37efa4c850.title: Wore a Golden Helmet in the armour slot
image.firsttorch.golden_helmet.descripti: Golden Helmet recipe: three Gold Ingots across the top and one on each side below.
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.pack.t: Pack for the First Nether Visit
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.pack.d:
Goal: assemble the minimum equipment.

Bring an Iron, Diamond, or Netherite Sword and Pickaxe, a Shield, Flint and Steel, 32 Cobblestone, 16 Torches, and eight filling cooked foods. Wear the Golden Helmet and your best other Armour. The automatic objectives remain recorded once observed, so recheck the actual kit before entry.

Put Shield, Sword, Pickaxe, Cobblestone, Torches, and food in easy-to-reach slots. Water cannot be placed normally in the Nether; leave the Bucket at home and keep several inventory slots free.

Reward: Four Bread for the journey.
task.firsttorch.135a6f7bc3e80294.title: Hold 1 Sword made of Iron or better
task.firsttorch.246b708cd4f913a5.title: Hold 1 Pickaxe made of Iron or better
task.firsttorch.357c819de50a24b6.title: Hold 1 Shield
task.firsttorch.468d92aef61b35c7.title: Hold 1 Flint and Steel
task.firsttorch.579ea3bf072c46d8.title: Hold 32 Cobblestone
task.firsttorch.68afb4c0183d57e9.title: Hold 16 Torches
task.firsttorch.79b0c5d1294e68fa.title: Hold 8 filling cooked foods
image.firsttorch.iron_sword.description: Iron Sword recipe: two Iron Ingots above one Stick.
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.activa:
Goal: activate the Nether Portal without entering it.

Check the Golden Helmet and kit, then stand in front of the frame. Right-click the top of either lower Obsidian block with Flint and Steel. A correct frame fills with purple portal surface.

If ordinary fire appears, extinguish it with the left mouse button and check the 4 × 5 frame, ten ordinary Obsidian, and clear opening. Do not touch the purple surface; standing in it starts the dimension change.

Set the checkmark while you remain safely outside.

Reward: 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.3ce3f8045c7192bd.title: Activated the portal without entering
image.firsttorch.nether_portal_lit.descr: Activated Nether Portal with a purple portal surface inside the frame.
quest.firsttorch.nether_equipment.secure:
Goal: secure the area around the Overworld side of the active portal.

Light the ground in front of and behind the portal and the route home. Fill holes, protect nearby drops, and keep a level two-block-high arrival area clear on both sides.

Do not enclose the exit or put blocks in the purple surface. The portal does not set surroundings on fire; this work prevents falls and makes the return route clear.

Set the checkmark when both sides and the route home are clear and lit.

Reward: Eight Torches and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.6f16b2370ca4d95e.title: Secured and lit the Overworld side of the portal
Goal: check your return route and condition immediately before entering for the first time.

Check your Bed at home; sleep there at night to set respawn, and never bring it into the Nether. Record the Overworld portal coordinates with F3. Store unneeded valuables, fill Hunger, recover health, and leave inventory space.

Final check: Golden Helmet and other Armour, Shield in offhand, and Sword, Pickaxe, Cobblestone, Torches, food, and Flint and Steel in reachable slots.

Set the checkmark only after this complete check.

Reward: Two Bread as return reserve.
task.firsttorch.235af67b40e81d92.title: Completed the full departure check
chapter.firsttorch.nether_arrival.title: First Nether Arrival
chapter.firsttorch.nether_arrival.descri: Enter carefully, secure the portal shelter, and return safely once.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_arrival.title: Safe First Return
trophy.firsttorch.nether_arrival.descrip: You secured the Nether portal area and returned safely to the Overworld.
quest.firsttorch.nether_arrival.step.tit: The First Step into the Nether
quest.firsttorch.nether_arrival.step.des:
Goal: enter the Nether for the first time and remain directly beside the portal.

Walk into the purple surface and remain there until the dimension change begins. After loading, release every movement key and look around before taking a step.

Step carefully out but stay directly beside the portal. Sneak near an edge. Do not enter a dark passage, walk across unknown ground, or attack any creature. If Lava, a drop, or an enemy is immediately dangerous, return through the same portal.

Minecraft detects the first entry automatically. Set the additional checkmark only when you are safely beside the visible portal.

Reward: 16 Cobblestone and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.568d29ae731b40c5.title: Entered the Nether
task.firsttorch.679e3abf042c51d6.title: Stopped safely beside the visible portal
quest.firsttorch.nether_arrival.look.des:
Goal: inspect the immediate surroundings without moving away from the portal.

Check the block under your feet, then floor, walls, and ceiling. Look for Lava, fire, drops, falling Gravel, tight spaces, and nearby enemies. If the place is dangerous, return to the Overworld; retreat is correct.

The Golden Helmet calms ordinary Piglins only while you avoid attacks and guarded blocks. From safe cover, place a few Cobblestone blocks and Torches without blocking the purple surface.

Set the checkmark after surveying the area and either returning safely or placing initial cover.

Reward: Eight Cobblestone and four Torches.
task.firsttorch.23d27e384fa506b1.title: Inspected the portal area and placed initial cover
Goal: enclose the Nether side of the portal in a small, lit Cobblestone room.

Close holes around the frame before widening narrow ground. Build Cobblestone walls and a closed roof; it protects the return route from ordinary Ghast fireballs.

Keep a clear two-block-high space on both sides of the purple surface and a protected exit to safe ground. Light the interior, but do not put blocks in the portal or use Water or a Bed in the Nether.

Set the checkmark once floor, walls, roof, lighting, and usable exit are complete.

Reward: 32 Cobblestone and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.6716b27c83e94af5.title: Built a lit Cobblestone shelter with an exit
quest.firsttorch.nether_arrival.return.t: Mark the Portal and Return Route
quest.firsttorch.nether_arrival.return.d:
Goal: record Nether coordinates, mark the exit, and return to the Overworld once.

Record the portal X, Y, and Z with F3. A normal Compass does not point reliably home in the Nether without a Lodestone; use written coordinates and visible markers.

Mark the exit with Torches or Cobblestone without narrowing it. For a route marker, stack two Cobblestone and attach a Torch to the side pointing back toward the portal. Use markers only in safe, visible places.

Return through the purple surface, confirm the original Overworld portal and the route home, then set the checkmark.

Reward: Four Bread and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.235af6b0c72d8e39.title: Marked the Nether portal and returned to the Overworld
image.firsttorch.nether_route_marker.des: Nether route marker: a two-block Cobblestone post with a Torch on the side pointing back to the portal.
chapter.firsttorch.nether_safety.title: A Safe Marked Nether Route
chapter.firsttorch.nether_safety.descrip: Practise a short marked route, recognise dangers, and return in time.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_safety.title: Marked Route Completed
trophy.firsttorch.nether_safety.descript: You explored a short marked Nether route and returned safely.
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.shelter.d:
Goal: return prepared to the Nether and initially remain inside the secured portal shelter.

Store unneeded valuables, fill Hunger and health, and check recorded Nether portal coordinates. Wear the Golden Helmet and other Armour; damage, not walking, wears the Helmet.

Keep Shield, Sword, Pickaxe, Cobblestone, Torches, and food reachable, including six Cobblestone and three Torches for markers. After loading, release movement keys and open the exit only when no enemy or fireball is directly outside.

Set the checkmark when fully equipped inside the closed lit shelter.
task.firsttorch.347c19e2fa50b16d.title: Returned fully equipped to the portal shelter
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.piglins.t: Not Every Piglin Is the Same
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.piglins.d:
Goal: distinguish ordinary Piglins, Piglin Brutes, and Zombified Piglins.

Gold Armour stops ordinary Piglins attacking merely because you are present, but does not make you invulnerable. Attacks, guarded containers, and mining Gold can still anger them.

Piglin Brutes carry Golden Axes and always attack; Gold does not help. Zombified Piglins are usually peaceful until one is attacked, which can anger many nearby. Never attack to identify them; keep distance and return to shelter when unsure.

Set the checkmark once you can explain these reactions.

Reward: Four Torches.
task.firsttorch.569e3b041c72d38f.title: I know the three important Piglin reactions
image.firsttorch.piglin_comparison.descr: Comparison of ordinary Piglin, Piglin Brute, Baby Piglin, and Zombified Piglin; only the adult ordinary Piglin is a later barter partner.
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.hazards.t: Cover from Ghasts, Fire, and Lava
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.hazards.d:
Goal: know the safe response to hazards outside the shelter.

A Ghast's fireball explodes and may leave fire. Do not return it on this first route: move behind closed Cobblestone cover or beneath the roof. Extinguish reachable single fire with the left mouse button, but never cross a ledge or approach Lava.

Lava flows faster and farther here. Do not mine carelessly beside it or bridge an open Lava field; Water cannot be placed as rescue. Inspect briefly from cover and retreat when a direction is unsafe.

Set the checkmark after this safety review.

Reward: Eight Cobblestone.
task.firsttorch.08105d263e94f5a1.title: Understood the Ghast, fire, and Lava response
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.route.des:
Goal: travel no farther than three safe markers, then return to the shelter.

The automatic tasks confirm six Cobblestone and three Torches were available. Leave only when the exit is clear. Stack two Cobblestone and attach a Torch on the side pointing back to the portal; keep each marker visible from the previous one.

Do not mine Gold, open containers, enter structures, cross Lava, or pursue enemies. Turn earlier when needed; safety matters more than three markers. Follow Torch sides back and set the checkmark inside the lit shelter.

Reward: Two Bread.
task.firsttorch.2a327f4850b617c3.title: Hold 6 Cobblestone for three route markers
task.firsttorch.3b43805961c728d4.title: Hold 3 Torches for three route markers
task.firsttorch.4c54916a72d839e5.title: Travelled a marked route safely and returned to the shelter
quest.firsttorch.nether_safety.return.de:
Goal: return through the original portal to the Overworld and finish the first Nether route.

Check health and route in the shelter, leaving markers standing for a later safe visit. Return through the purple surface, confirm the original portal and lit route home, then store finds, replenish food, and replace damaged gear.

An early retreat because of danger is not failure. Set the checkmark once safely back at the original Overworld portal.

Reward: 10 XP.
task.firsttorch.6e76b38c94fa5b07.title: Returned safely through the original portal
chapter.firsttorch.piglin_barter.title: Piglin Bartering (Optional)
chapter.firsttorch.piglin_barter.descrip: Learn one careful optional Piglin barter; no particular result is guaranteed.
trophy.firsttorch.piglin_barter.title: Careful Barter
trophy.firsttorch.piglin_barter.descript: You completed one careful Piglin barter and returned safely.
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.intro.tit: What to Do in the Nether?
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.intro.des:
Goal: understand the optional Nether activities and choose only prepared paths.

The first marked route is complete. Optional Piglin bartering and short resource trips do not block later paths. Nether Fortresses need stronger preparation; Bastion Remnants are advanced and dangerous even with Gold Armour.

Set the checkmark once you understand the structure. You do not need to leave the Overworld.
task.firsttorch.18216e374fa506b3.title: I know the planned Nether paths
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.gold.titl: Optional: One Gold Ingot to Barter
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.gold.desc:
Goal: hold one Gold Ingot for a voluntary Piglin barter.

An adult ordinary Piglin takes exactly one Gold Ingot, waits briefly, then throws back a random item or stack. There is no trade screen and no selectable result. Gold Nuggets do not work.

Baby Piglins, Piglin Brutes, and Zombified Piglins do not provide normal bartering. This is optional: if no safe partner is available, continue later.

The task completes automatically with one Gold Ingot.
task.firsttorch.0098d5aeb61c7d29.title: Hold 1 Gold Ingot for the first Piglin barter
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.place.des:
Goal: find a safe place beside an adult ordinary Piglin on the known marked route.

Wear the Golden Helmet and repeat the equipment check. Use firm level ground, a clear retreat to the shelter, and nearby Cobblestone cover; avoid Lava, fire, drops, Bastions, guarded containers, and Gold Blocks.

Check from a distance that the Piglin is adult and ordinary. A Brute, Baby Piglin, or Zombified Piglin is not a partner. Do not lure one into the Overworld.

Set the checkmark only after checking Helmet, Piglin, ground, cover, and retreat.
task.firsttorch.22baf7c0d83e9f4b.title: Found a safe place beside an adult ordinary Piglin
quest.firsttorch.piglin_barter.trade.des:
Goal: give exactly one Gold Ingot to an adult ordinary Piglin, collect the result safely, and return.

Hold one Gold Ingot in the main hand, aim at the checked Piglin, and right-click once. Do not attack, touch guarded blocks, or give another Ingot while it examines the first.

It throws a random result: it may be Blackstone, Gravel, Obsidian, Quartz, Iron Nuggets, Ender Pearls, or a Fire Resistance Potion, but nothing is guaranteed. Do not chase an item toward a drop, fire, or Lava.

Follow markers back to the shelter and return home. Set the checkmark after a completed safe barter and return.

Reward: One Gold Ingot and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.44dc19e2fa50b16d.title: Completed one safe Piglin barter and returned
chapter.firsttorch.nether_resources.desc: Take a short marked trip for Netherrack and Quartz, then bring both samples home.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_resources.title: Resources Returned Safely
trophy.firsttorch.nether_resources.descr: You returned Netherrack and Nether Quartz safely to the Overworld.
quest.firsttorch.nether_resources.plan.d:
Goal: choose a safe nearby mining place along your marked route.

Bring an Iron Pickaxe or better, Golden Helmet, Shield, Flint and Steel, cooked food, Torches, and Cobblestone. Keep to the marked route, with firm ground, cover, and a clear retreat.

Netherrack and Quartz occur in every Nether biome. Ignore Gold, high Glowstone, and unfamiliar structures. Retreat if Ghasts, Piglin Brutes, fire, or Lava threaten the way home.

Set the checkmark after checking equipment, footing, cover, and retreat.
task.firsttorch.2d94a1b35e7fa28c.title: I checked a safe nearby mining place
quest.firsttorch.nether_resources.nether:
Goal: collect 16 Netherrack at the checked mining place.

Netherrack is common red Nether stone and breaks very quickly with a Pickaxe. Mine visible individual blocks from firm ground; never dig straight down or blindly upward, because Lava, cavities, or drops may hide behind it.

Fire on Netherrack burns until extinguished. Put out one reachable flame with a left click, but retreat if it spreads or cannot be reached safely.

The task completes automatically with 16 Netherrack. Keep Cobblestone for clear cover and markers.
task.firsttorch.4fb6c3d57091a4ae.title: Hold 16 Netherrack in the inventory at once
quest.firsttorch.nether_resources.quartz:
Goal: collect four Nether Quartz.

Quartz Ore has bright white inclusions in Netherrack. Search only safe walls reachable from the ground. Mine without Silk Touch: it drops Quartz and experience; Silk Touch drops the Ore block instead.

Never enlarge dangerous cavities for another Ore. Four Quartz are enough, and this optional quest can wait if the safe route has none. Quartz is useful later for bright blocks and Redstone components.

The task completes automatically with four Quartz.
task.firsttorch.61d8e5f792b3c6c0.title: Hold 4 Nether Quartz in the inventory at once
quest.firsttorch.nether_resources.return:
Goal: return through the original portal with Netherrack and Nether Quartz.

End the trip while the marked route is safe. Follow the Torch sides to the shelter, check that nothing followed, then return through the same portal and store both samples at home.

Do not delay retreat for one more Ore or experience. Set the checkmark in the Overworld after safe storage and checking that the route remains usable.

Reward: Eight Cobblestone and 5 XP.
task.firsttorch.03fa0719b4d5e8e2.title: I returned safely to the Overworld with both samples
chapter.firsttorch.nether_fortress.title: Nether Fortress Preparation
chapter.firsttorch.nether_fortress.descr: Prepare carefully, find a Fortress, and establish a safe retreat before fighting.
trophy.firsttorch.nether_fortress.title: Fortress Ready
trophy.firsttorch.nether_fortress.descri: You prepared a safe Fortress approach and retreat, not a completed victory.
quest.firsttorch.nether_fortress.equipme: Equip Yourself for the Nether Fortress

Goal: prepare the minimum kit for a Fortress search.

Bring an Iron-or-better Sword and Pickaxe, Shield, 64 Cobblestone, and 16 substantial cooked foods. Wear the Golden Helmet and Iron-or-better Chestplate, Leggings, and Boots. Also take Flint and Steel, 32 Torches, and markers.

Sleep, record portal and shelter coordinates, start healthy and fed, and store valuables. Automatic objectives remain sticky, so physically recheck the complete kit.

Set the checkmark only after the worn armour and reserve check.
task.firsttorch.36ad35cca4724357.title: Hold 1 Iron-or-better Sword
task.firsttorch.1b63a993ed3c4db3.title: Hold 1 Iron-or-better Pickaxe
task.firsttorch.3e4af2d781ec4b57.title: Hold 1 Shield
task.firsttorch.65c89337665c4e28.title: Hold 64 Cobblestone
task.firsttorch.21d6ce3ad23a412b.title: Hold 16 substantial cooked foods
task.firsttorch.5583fd1f127a4b12.title: Golden Helmet and Iron-or-better armour worn; reserve checked
quest.firsttorch.nether_fortress.find.de:
Goal: find a Fortress without losing the safe route home.

Fortresses use dark-red Nether Bricks, long bridges, pillars, and corridors; black Blackstone Bastions are not the target. Extend known markers carefully, record turns, and keep Torch sides pointing home.

Do not cross open Lava or force a dangerous route. The search can take several trips. Set the checkmark after reaching Nether Bricks, recording coordinates, and checking a marked retreat; do not go deep inside yet.

Reward: 5 experience points for locating the Fortress and checking the return route.
task.firsttorch.22d566f202a7429e.title: I found a Nether Fortress with a safe retreat
image.firsttorch.nether_fortress.descrip: In-game screenshot of a Nether Fortress with Nether Brick bridges and supporting pillars; brightened for visibility.
quest.firsttorch.nether_fortress.entranc:
Goal: build a protected retreat room at the Fortress edge.

Use firm ground connected to your marked route. Build a closed, lit Cobblestone room with roof and marked outside. Leave a two-block-high passage: you pass, but taller Wither Skeletons cannot.

Record its coordinates and inspect only the adjoining corridor from this retreat. Torches mark routes but do not make a Fortress safe. Set the checkmark after checking roof, floor, route, barrier, and blocks.
task.firsttorch.0f3b0653610d483b.title: I have a protected and marked Fortress entrance
quest.firsttorch.nether_fortress.hazards:
Goal: know the hazards before fighting.

Blazes fire volleys; a full Cobblestone wall breaks line of sight. Wither Skeletons are tall, use Stone Swords, and inflict Wither; retreat through the two-block barrier and never fight on bridge edges. Other enemies and drops can hide around corners.

If several hazards meet, block the opening and return home. Set the checkmark in the retreat room after naming safe reactions for Blazes, Wither Skeletons, and crowded corridors.
task.firsttorch.54a8aa81d49e4187.title: I know solid cover, the two-block barrier, and full retreat
image.firsttorch.fortress_hazards.descri: Fortress hazards: Blaze, Wither Skeleton, and Magma Cube.
chapter.firsttorch.fortress_return.title: Fortress Return and Brewing Supplies
chapter.firsttorch.fortress_return.descr: Collect the first brewing supplies in a secured Fortress, then bring them safely home.
trophy.firsttorch.fortress_return.title: Fortress Supplies Returned
trophy.firsttorch.fortress_return.descri: You brought Blaze Rods, Nether Wart, and Soul Sand safely home from a Fortress.
quest.firsttorch.fortress_return.blaze_r:
Goal: defeat Blazes carefully until two Blaze Rods are in your inventory at once.

First prepare a clear retreat behind a full Cobblestone corner. Do not fight on an exposed bridge. When one Blaze appears, move fully behind the wall during its burning attack phase and wait there for the fireballs.

If you cannot reach the wall, right-click to raise your Shield and face the Blaze directly. It blocks frontal fireballs, not shots from the side or behind, so solid cover remains safer. After the volley, use a Bow from cover or approach only on safe ground for one fully charged Sword strike. Never begin melee while several Blazes are visible or another enemy can approach behind you.

A caged block with a spinning Blaze is a Blaze Spawner. Do not stand beside it unprotected or destroy it yet; secure only an approach and retreat as soon as several Blazes appear. If burning, reach cover, watch Hearts, and eat when Hunger is missing. Blazes do not always drop a Rod: end the trip rather than continuing with damaged equipment. The task completes automatically with two Blaze Rods.
task.firsttorch.31ef76ac88474111.title: Hold 2 Blaze Rods in the inventory at once
image.firsttorch.blaze_spawner.descripti: A Blaze Spawner surrounded by several Blazes beneath a Fortress roof; retreat when several appear.
quest.firsttorch.fortress_return.wart.ti: Secure Nether Wart and Soul Sand
quest.firsttorch.fortress_return.wart.de:
Goal: collect four Nether Wart and four Soul Sand.

Some Fortresses have Nether Wart gardens beside staircases; not every Fortress has one. If this Fortress has none, search for another Fortress on a later prepared trip rather than entering a Bastion. Secure both ends of the corridor, floor, and ceiling before collecting anything.

Mature dark-red Wart drops several items. Take four Soul Sand blocks from beneath it too. Nether Wart grows on Soul Sand in any dimension without Water, Farmland, or special light. Both tasks complete automatically when all four of each are held at once.
task.firsttorch.0966e3da03134381.title: Hold 4 Nether Wart in the inventory at once
task.firsttorch.25df04566b784491.title: Hold 4 Soul Sand in the inventory at once
image.firsttorch.nether_wart_garden.desc: A Nether Wart garden beside a Fortress staircase.
Goal: bring Blaze Rods, Nether Wart, and Soul Sand home through the original portal.

Leave through the secured entrance and follow only your marked route. Repair damage only from cover; if it is blocked, retreat to the Fortress room instead of opening an unmarked shortcut.

At home, store both Rods safely. Plant one Nether Wart on each of four Soul Sand blocks in a protected place; Water is unnecessary. Set the checkmark only in the Overworld after the farm is planted and the Fortress route remains findable.

Reward: 16 Cobblestone and 10 XP.
task.firsttorch.4c2e1220ea4c4b18.title: Returned safely, stored the Rods, and planted a Nether Wart farm
command.firsttorch.claim_all.result: Claimed rewards for %s quests; %s still unclaimed.
chapter.firsttorch.brewing.title: Brewing Foundations
chapter.firsttorch.brewing.description: Set up a safe home brewing station, then make Awkward and Strength Potions step by step.
trophy.firsttorch.brewing.title: First Potion Brewer
trophy.firsttorch.brewing.description: You set up a safe brewing station and made your first Potion of Strength.
quest.firsttorch.brewing.place.title: Brew Safely at Home
quest.firsttorch.brewing.place.descripti:
Goal: choose a permanent brewing place in your Overworld base and understand the setup.

Brewing needs a Brewing Stand, Blaze Powder as fuel, Water Bottles, and one ingredient. The three bottle slots along the bottom brew together; the ingredient goes in the top slot.

Place the stand in a lit, protected room near your storage. Potions need no open flame, and a Brewing Stand cannot start a fire. The two Blaze Rods brought home are enough to begin: process only one into Powder; keep the other for the Stand.

Set the checkmark when the place is chosen and both Blaze Rods are still available.
task.firsttorch.1b7528e4cf936d0a.title: Brewing place chosen and 2 Blaze Rods checked
quest.firsttorch.brewing.powder.title: Make Blaze Powder
quest.firsttorch.brewing.powder.descript:
Goal: turn exactly one Blaze Rod into two Blaze Powder.

Put one Blaze Rod into any crafting slot. This shapeless recipe makes two Blaze Powder. Leave the second Rod untouched: it is required for the Brewing Stand next.

Blaze Powder has two jobs. In the left fuel slot it supplies up to 20 brewing operations; in the top ingredient slot it later turns Awkward Potions into Strength.

The automatic task completes when two Blaze Powder are in your inventory at once.
task.firsttorch.3d974a06e1b58f2c.title: Hold 2 Blaze Powder in your inventory at once
image.firsttorch.blaze_powder_recipe.des: Recipe: one Blaze Rod crafts into two Blaze Powder.
quest.firsttorch.brewing.stand.title: Build a Brewing Stand
quest.firsttorch.brewing.stand.descripti:
Goal: craft a Brewing Stand and place it at the prepared location.

Put the remaining Blaze Rod in the centre of the middle row. Fill the bottom row with three suitable stone materials; three Cobblestone are the simplest choice. Take the Stand from the result slot.

Wait briefly in game until the inventory task is confirmed. Then right-click a solid block to place it, then right-click the Stand to open it. The automatic task only checks that you hold one Stand, so place and open it before continuing.
task.firsttorch.5fb96c2803d7a14e.title: Hold 1 Brewing Stand
image.firsttorch.brewing_stand_recipe.de: Recipe: one Blaze Rod above three Cobblestone makes a Brewing Stand.
quest.firsttorch.brewing.bottles.title: Make Three Glass Bottles
quest.firsttorch.brewing.bottles.descrip:
Goal: craft three Glass Bottles for one complete brewing operation.

If Glass is missing, smelt Sand in a Furnace. Arrange three Glass in a V: left and right in the middle row, then one in the bottom centre. The recipe makes three Bottles.

After drinking an ordinary potion, its empty Glass Bottle remains. Store it near the Brewing Stand to refill and reuse.

The automatic task completes when three empty Glass Bottles are in your inventory at once.
task.firsttorch.71db8e4a25f9c360.title: Hold 3 Glass Bottles in your inventory at once
image.firsttorch.glass_bottle_recipe.des: Recipe: three Glass in a V makes three reusable Glass Bottles.
quest.firsttorch.brewing.water.title: Fill Three Water Bottles
quest.firsttorch.brewing.water.descripti:
Goal: fill all three Glass Bottles and put them into the three bottom slots of the Brewing Stand.

Hold a Glass Bottle and right-click a Water source block. Repeat for all three Bottles. A filled Cauldron also works, but loses water for every Bottle; a Water source is simpler.

Water Bottles do not stack. Open the Brewing Stand and right-click to place one Water Bottle into each of its three lower bottle slots. This is a placement exercise, not an inventory check. Prepare it in the Overworld: placed Water evaporates in the Nether.
task.firsttorch.23fda06c471be582.title: 3 Water Bottles are placed in the Brewing Stand
quest.firsttorch.brewing.awkward.title: Brew Awkward Potions
quest.firsttorch.brewing.awkward.descrip:
Goal: use one Nether Wart to turn the three Water Bottles into Awkward Potions.

Put Blaze Powder in the square fuel slot at upper left. It is consumed immediately and fills the yellow fuel bar with 20 charges. Put one Nether Wart in the top ingredient slot, then wait for the progress bar to finish.

Check that each bottom bottle is now named Awkward Potion. Then take one finished Awkward Potion out of the Stand and put it back into a bottom slot before continuing with Strength. Vanilla detects the generic first brewing advancement when a finished potion is taken out; it does not prove this exact potion variant or all three bottles. Previous advancement progress can also already satisfy the automatic task.

Awkward Potions have no effect by themselves, but are the foundation for useful potions.
task.firsttorch.451fc28e693d07a4.title: Take out a finished potion to trigger the first-brewing advancement
Brewing Stand with Water Bottles, Blaze Powder fuel, Nether Wart, and the progress bar for Awkward Potions.
quest.firsttorch.brewing.strength.title: Brew Your First Potion of Strength
quest.firsttorch.brewing.strength.descri:
Goal: turn the Awkward Potions into Potions of Strength, then drink one safely.

Leave the Awkward Potions in the bottom slots. With fuel still on the left, put another Blaze Powder in the top ingredient slot. One operation makes up to three three-minute Potions of Strength.

Hold one Potion of Strength and hold right-click until it is fully drunk. Press E to open your inventory and confirm the Strength effect icon and timer. Strength increases melee damage; it does not prevent fire or fall damage and does not replace Armour, a Shield, or cover.

The reward gives three Redstone Dust and ten XP points. Later, one Redstone Dust extends ordinary Strength to eight minutes; Glowstone Dust instead makes shorter Strength II. Fire Resistance is a later optional lesson, not part of this foundation.

Set the manual checkmark only after you actually drank Strength and saw its effect.
task.firsttorch.6731e4a08b5f29c6.title: I brewed and drank Strength and checked its effect
image.firsttorch.strength_potion_brewing: Brewing Stand turning Awkward Potions into Potions of Strength with Blaze Powder as the ingredient.
chapter.firsttorch.fire_resistance.title: Fire Resistance (optional)
chapter.firsttorch.fire_resistance.descr: Brew and store an optional safety reserve; it never unlocks Bastions or another required route.
trophy.firsttorch.fire_resistance.title: Fire-safe reserve
trophy.firsttorch.fire_resistance.descri: You prepared a careful Fire Resistance reserve.
quest.firsttorch.fire_resistance.intro.d:
Goal: consciously decide whether to begin the optional Fire Resistance branch now.

Fire Resistance prevents damage from fire, Lava, Magma Blocks, and Blaze fire attacks while it lasts. This makes it a powerful extra safeguard for later Nether trips.

The Potion does not protect against melee attacks, arrows, explosions, falls, suffocation, or falling into the Void. It replaces neither Armour and a Shield nor solid cover and a marked retreat.

This Potion needs Magma Cream. Obtaining it may require another Nether trip or a Slimeball and additional Blaze Powder. The entire branch therefore remains optional and blocks no later main quest.

Set the checkmark when you understand its benefit and limits and voluntarily want to begin obtaining the ingredient.
task.firsttorch.2ea57905b824d6f1.title: I know its benefit, limits, and optional nature
quest.firsttorch.fire_resistance.cream.d:
Goal: hold one Magma Cream without forcing an unprepared trip.

The controlled crafting route is shapeless: place one Slimeball and one Blaze Powder in any crafting slots. You may first need to retrieve another Blaze Rod from the already secured Nether Fortress and process it into Powder.

Alternatively, medium and large Magma Cubes can drop Magma Cream; small ones cannot, and a larger Cube does not guarantee a drop. Do not make an unprepared search for one particular Nether biome.

Fight a Magma Cube only on broad solid ground from a closed retreat room. It splits into smaller Cubes when defeated. Keep the exit blockable and attack each Cube separately with fully charged strikes.

The automatic task completes when one Magma Cream is in your inventory. Its source does not matter.
task.firsttorch.40c79b27da46f813.title: Hold 1 Magma Cream
image.firsttorch.magma_cream_recipe.desc: Recipe: one Slimeball and one Blaze Powder make Magma Cream.
quest.firsttorch.fire_resistance.brew.de:
Goal: brew up to three Potions of Fire Resistance with a duration of three minutes.

Fill up to three Glass Bottles with Water and first brew them with Nether Wart into Awkward Potions. Your Brewing Stand's yellow fuel bar should still hold charges; if it does not, load new Blaze Powder into the upper-left slot.

Leave the Awkward Potions at the bottom and put one Magma Cream into the ingredient slot at the upper centre. After one operation, every inserted bottle becomes a three-minute Potion of Fire Resistance at the same time.

Do not take the Potions into Lava merely to test them. Store at least one beside the Brewing Stand and set the checkmark after verifying its name and three-minute duration in the inventory.
task.firsttorch.62e9bd49fc681a35.title: I brewed Fire Resistance and checked 3:00
image.firsttorch.fire_resistance_brewing: Brewing Stand turning Awkward Potions into Fire Resistance with Magma Cream.
Goal: extend your Potions of Fire Resistance to eight minutes with one Redstone Dust.

Leave the ordinary Potions of Fire Resistance at the bottom of the Brewing Stand and place one Redstone Dust at the top as the ingredient. After brewing, the Bottles show Fire Resistance with a duration of eight minutes.

Redstone extends only the duration; Fire Resistance has no stronger Glowstone tier. Drink the Potion immediately before a prepared Nether trip and watch its effect icon and timer. Milk removes the effect immediately.

Do not test the Potion by deliberately jumping into Lava. It is a reserve for mistakes, not a new way to travel. If you fall in accidentally, stay calm, swim to the nearest solid edge, and leave the Nether before the timer ends.

Set the checkmark after at least one Potion shows eight minutes and is stored safely with your travel equipment.

Reward: five experience points mark this optional safety upgrade.
task.firsttorch.04abde6b1e8a3c57.title: At least 1 Fire Resistance Potion shows 8:00 and is stored
image.firsttorch.long_fire_resistance_br: Brewing Stand extending Fire Resistance with Redstone Dust.
chapter.firsttorch.ender_eyes.title: Eyes of Ender
chapter.firsttorch.ender_eyes.descriptio: Prepare, count and safely store Eyes before beginning the Stronghold search.
trophy.firsttorch.ender_eyes.title: Eyes prepared
trophy.firsttorch.ender_eyes.description: You made and stored a measured Eye reserve.
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.prepare.titl: Prepare the path to the End
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.prepare.desc:
Goal: understand the next material step without throwing an Eye of Ender yet.

The route to the End dimension passes through an End Portal in an underground Overworld Stronghold. Eyes of Ender later help locate it and fill its twelve portal frames. Each Eye needs one Ender Pearl and one Blaze Powder.

This chapter only prepares a reliable supply. The long search, safe digging into the Stronghold, and portal room follow in their own section. Until then, do not throw away Ender Pearls or Eyes of Ender out of curiosity.

Set the checkmark when you understand the difference between preparing materials and the later search.
task.firsttorch.1d864af6c0a47e2b.title: I am saving Pearls and Eyes for now
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.source.title: Choose an Ender Pearl source
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.source.descr:
Goal: choose a supply method suited to your world and experience.

Endermen are normally neutral. They attack only after you look directly at their face or attack them yourself. Look at their legs instead and avoid starting a fight accidentally.

A defeated Enderman can drop zero or one Ender Pearl. The Looting enchantment on a Sword can increase the maximum, but still does not guarantee a drop. Fight only when prepared: stand beneath a roof exactly two blocks high, keep a clear retreat, and attack from there with fully charged strikes. Endermen are nearly three blocks tall and cannot fit beneath that roof.

An adult ordinary Piglin can randomly give two to four Ender Pearls while bartering, but that result is not guaranteed. Use only the previously explained safe barter place, keep Gold Armour equipped, and preserve the marked retreat.

An experienced Cleric can also offer one Ender Pearl for five Emeralds. If your world already has a suitable Village and this trade, it is the safest route; this lesson does not require training a new Villager.

A thrown Ender Pearl teleports you when it lands, deals two and a half hearts of damage, and can rarely spawn an Endermite. Do not throw a Pearl from the supply you still need.

Set the checkmark after choosing at least one realistic route. You may combine them.
task.firsttorch.3fa86c18e2c6904d.title: I chose a safe source
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.pearls.title: Collect sixteen Ender Pearls
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.pearls.descr:
Goal: hold sixteen Ender Pearls in your inventory at the same time.

Collect Pearls through one or more of the chosen routes. Return home after small stages and store each find instead of carrying the whole supply through one risky fight or Nether trip.

The later portal has twelve frames. Some may already contain Eyes, but the plan does not rely on that. The four additional Pearls form a small initial search reserve.

The automatic task completes when sixteen Ender Pearls are in your inventory at the same time.

Wait in game until the inventory task is confirmed before processing the materials further.
task.firsttorch.51ca8e3a04e8b26f.title: Hold 16 Ender Pearls at once
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.powder.title: Collect sixteen Blaze Powder
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.powder.descr:
Goal: hold sixteen Blaze Powder in your inventory at the same time.

One Blaze Rod shapelessly makes two Blaze Powder, so sixteen Powder needs eight Rods. Use the already secured Nether Fortress, marked route home, full Armour, Shield, solid cover, and several short trips when that is safer.

Store extra Blaze Powder for your Brewing Stand separately. All sixteen units for this task will soon become Eyes of Ender.

The automatic task completes when sixteen Blaze Powder are in your inventory at the same time.

Wait in game until the inventory task is confirmed before processing the materials further.
task.firsttorch.73eca05c260ad481.title: Hold 16 Blaze Powder at once
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.craft.title: Craft sixteen Eyes of Ender
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.craft.descri:
Goal: combine your complete supply into sixteen Eyes of Ender.

The recipe is shapeless. Put Ender Pearls and an equal number of Blaze Powder into any crafting slots; each pair produces one Eye of Ender. The recipe works in the small inventory grid or at a Crafting Table.

Do not confuse the items: Ender Pearls teleport you, while Eyes of Ender locate a Stronghold and later fill the portal frames. Do not throw the finished Eyes yet; the next chapter plans the search and reserve together.

The automatic task completes when sixteen Eyes of Ender are in your inventory at the same time.

Wait in game until the inventory task is confirmed before processing the materials further.
task.firsttorch.250ec27e482cf6a3.title: Hold 16 Eyes of Ender at once
image.firsttorch.ender_eye_recipe.descri: Recipe: an Ender Pearl and Blaze Powder make an Eye of Ender.
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.store.title: Store the Eyes ready for travel
quest.firsttorch.ender_eyes.store.descri:
Goal: store all Eyes together and understand why the number is not a guarantee.

A complete End Portal has twelve frames. Some frames may already contain an Eye. When an Eye is later thrown to search, it usually drops as an item again, but it has a twenty-percent chance to shatter.

Sixteen Eyes are therefore a sensible starting supply, not a guarantee for every distance and random outcome. If fewer than twelve remain during the later search, pause the journey and make more.

Until the search quest begins, put the Eyes in one permanent Chest beside your travel equipment. Set the checkmark only after all sixteen are stored together and cannot accidentally be carried as ordinary throwables.

Reward: two additional Eyes of Ender enlarge the first search reserve; ten experience points recognise the demanding preparation.
task.firsttorch.4720e4a06a4e18c5.title: 16 Eyes stored together and safely
chapter.firsttorch.stronghold_search.des: Pack, search in careful stages, find the Stronghold and secure its entrance.
trophy.firsttorch.stronghold_search.desc: You located and secured a reliable Stronghold entrance.
Goal: prepare for a long Overworld journey with a reliable route home.

Bring at least a full set of Iron Armour or better, a Shield, an Iron Sword and Iron Pickaxe or better tools, a Water Bucket, 32 Torches, 64 Cobblestone, and 16 filling cooked foods. Pack at least the sixteen crafted Eyes of Ender; after claiming the reward, eighteen are available.

Sleep at home before leaving, record your base coordinates, and store valuables that are not needed. In the Overworld, a Compass points to world spawn rather than automatically pointing to your Bed or the Stronghold, so the coordinate note remains important.

A Stronghold may be far away. Plan several daylight stages, sleep only in a protected place, and never run blindly after the flight direction at night. You may turn back and continue later at any time.

Set the checkmark after equipment, supplies, and home coordinates are ready.
task.firsttorch.6b42f6c28c603ae7.title: Equipment, supplies, and home coordinates are ready
quest.firsttorch.stronghold_search.first:
Goal: establish the first search direction without losing sight of the Eye.

In daylight, find a clear and safe area without dense leaves, a high wall, Lava, or a steep drop. Hold one Eye of Ender and right-click once. The Eye rises and flies a short distance towards the nearest Stronghold.

Stay still and watch the entire flight. After a short time, the Eye usually falls as an item; sometimes it shatters. Pick up a fallen Eye immediately and check the remaining supply.

Record the approximate compass direction and the coordinates of the throw. Set the checkmark only after exactly one controlled throw and either recovery or a confirmed shatter.
task.firsttorch.0d6418e4ae825c09.title: First throw observed, direction recorded, stock checked
image.firsttorch.ender_eye_search.descri: An Eye of Ender leading a careful surface search.
quest.firsttorch.stronghold_search.stage:
Goal: approach the Stronghold with a few observed throws and a documented route home.

Travel several hundred blocks in the indicated direction, or stop sooner when terrain, night, or enemies require it. Mark important turns, record coordinates regularly, and keep track of food and the return route.

Throw only one Eye from each new clear area. Recover it and adjust direction. Do not throw while sprinting, beneath trees, over Water, beside cliffs, or during combat; the Eye is easily lost there.

If a later Eye clearly points back, you passed the target. Return between the final two throw locations and check at shorter intervals. When fewer than twelve Eyes remain, stop the search, return home safely, and make replacements.

Set the checkmark once several documented stages have visibly narrowed the search.
task.firsttorch.2f863a06c0a47e2b.title: Search route narrowed in safe stages
quest.firsttorch.stronghold_search.targe:
Goal: identify a small surface search area before digging.

Near the Stronghold, a thrown Eye no longer flies far ahead and instead travels noticeably downward. Throw from two or three nearby clear points, recover every surviving Eye, and compare directions. This narrows the area without digging immediately at the first point.

Build a clearly visible surface marker, record its coordinates, and secure the area for a later return. Sleep in a protected outpost when necessary, but do not lose the home coordinates.

Never dig straight down. Caves, Lava, or occupied rooms may lie beneath you. Set the checkmark when the target area is marked and a safe staircase starting point has been chosen.
task.firsttorch.41a85c28e2c6904d.title: Target area marked and safe staircase chosen
quest.firsttorch.stronghold_search.reach:
Goal: dig down a safe staircase and reach the Stronghold.

Begin a little beside the marked target and dig a broad staircase down. Never stand directly on the block being removed. Light the route, close side caves at first, and keep the Water Bucket, Shield, and Cobblestone accessible.

Use another individual Eye only when the staircase appears likely to miss the target. An Eye that flies upward or back while underground shows that you passed the suitable height or direction.

Strongholds commonly contain Stone Bricks, Mossy Stone Bricks, and Cracked Stone Bricks. Do not open a found wall at head height: first create a protected standing place, then make a small opening through which the room can be observed.

Silverfish can emerge from infested blocks in the Stronghold and awaken more Silverfish. If one appears, retreat to the staircase, block the passage, and do not fight blindly inside an unknown room.

Reaching the Stronghold is detected automatically through the Vanilla advancement. Do not search for the portal room yet; secure the entrance first.
task.firsttorch.63ca7e4a04e8b26f.title: Reach an Overworld Stronghold for the first time
quest.firsttorch.stronghold_search.secur:
Goal: make the first Stronghold entrance safe and return to the surface once.

Build a small lit retreat room at the opening with a closable passage. Mark the staircase clearly and record the entrance coordinates and depth. Do not spread route markers through unknown Stronghold corridors yet.

Climb your staircase all the way back to the surface. Check the marker, time of day, supplies, and route home there. Exploring the maze becomes reasonable only after this return route works.

Set the checkmark after successfully returning to the surface. The next chapter explains doors, corridors, Silverfish, Libraries, and the portal room separately.

Reward: sixteen Torches replace part of the route lighting; ten experience points recognise the safe location process.
task.firsttorch.05ec906c260ad481.title: Entrance secured, coordinates recorded, and surface reached again
chapter.firsttorch.stronghold_interior.d: Mark safe routes, understand Iron Doors and recognise hazards. The Library remains optional.
chapter.firsttorch.portal_room.title: Secure the Portal Room
chapter.firsttorch.portal_room.descripti: Find and secure the portal room, count its empty frames and return home before activation.
chapter.firsttorch.end_preparation.title: Ready for the End
chapter.firsttorch.end_preparation.descr: Check equipment and the return point, activate the portal and remain safely in the Overworld.
trophy.firsttorch.stronghold_interior.de: You checked Stronghold routes, Iron Doors and hazards, and made the optional Library decision.
trophy.firsttorch.portal_room.title: Twelve Frames, One Plan
trophy.firsttorch.portal_room.descriptio: You secured the portal room, counted the missing Eyes and returned safely home with the note.
trophy.firsttorch.end_preparation.title: Ready Before the Portal
